s1.syndrome_frame: Worsening skin condition with systemic symptoms in a patient with a history of autoimmune disorders
salient_findings: Diffuse ill-defined erythema and mild edema of the face and eyelids
Violaceous to erythematous patches on the joints, periungual skin, and chest
Scaly erythematous plaques on lateral leg
key_facts: Patient has a history of biopsy-proven psoriasis
Patient has a history of juvenile dermatomyositis (DM)
Juvenile DM had been in remission for several years
Patient previously treated with adalimumab, etanercept, methotrexate, guselkumab, ustekinumab, and topical corticosteroids
Patient experienced fatigue, difficulty picking up her child, and climbing stairs after starting new medication
Physical examination revealed diffuse ill-defined erythema and mild edema of the face and eyelids
Laboratory evaluation results were negative or normal, including creatine kinase levels and aldolase levels

shortlist.label: Dermatomyositis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of biopsy-proven juvenile dermatomyositis and presents with worsening skin condition and systemic symptoms

shortlist.label: Psoriasis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of biopsy-proven psoriasis and presents with scaly erythematous plaques

shortlist.label: Lupus erythematosus
shortlist.why_kept: Patient presents with systemic symptoms and skin manifestations that could be consistent with lupus

shortlist.label: Amyopathic dermatomyositis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient presents with skin manifestations of dermatomyositis without significant muscle involvement

shortlist.label: Mixed connective tissue disease
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of autoimmune disorders and presents with overlapping features of different connective tissue diseases

raw.rationale: The patient has a history of juvenile dermatomyositis and presents with skin manifestations such as diffuse ill-defined erythema, mild edema, and violaceous to erythematous patches, but normal creatine kinase and aldolase levels, indicating no active muscle involvement, which is consistent with amyopathic dermatomyositis.

rejected.label: Dermatomyositis
rejected.why: Normal creatine kinase and aldolase levels suggest no active muscle involvement, which is a key feature of dermatomyositis.

rejected.label: Psoriasis
rejected.why: While the patient has a history of psoriasis, the current presentation of skin manifestations and other symptoms is more consistent with amyopathic dermatomyositis.

rejected.label: Lupus erythematosus
rejected.why: There is no mention of other systemic symptoms or laboratory findings typical of lupus erythematosus, such as joint pain, kidney involvement, or positive autoantibodies.

rejected.label: Mixed connective tissue disease
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and laboratory findings do not meet the criteria for mixed connective tissue disease, which typically includes a combination of features from lupus, scleroderma, and polymyositis/dermatomyositis.

rejected.label: Psoriasis
rejected.why: The presence of skin manifestations such as photodistributed poikiloderma and violaceous to erythematous patches are more suggestive of amyopathic dermatomyositis than psoriasis alone.
